documents.title: University Guidelines for AI Use in the Classroom (provost announcement)
documents.summary: A December 2025 Provost announcement of UMBC's advisory guidelines for AI in teaching and administration. It says the guidelines are not a policy, leaves the decision to each instructor, offers a green/yellow/red traffic-light model and asks only for a clear syllabus statement. Only the announcement was retrievable, not the full guidelines.
documents.stance_why: Both coders: delegates. The announcement says "these guidelines are not a policy" and "Faculty retain full discretion to determine whether, how, and when AI tools are used in their courses", and offers a traffic-light model of "permissible, limited, or prohibited uses" for instructors, so the document sets no stance itself and lists tiers.

units.why: "developed through broad consultation between faculty and staff and reflect emerging best practices and examples from peer institutions" describes how the guidelines were made, which is P84.
units.anchor: developed through broad consultation between faculty and staff
units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on P84, admin, before-course, informs for the consultation clause. Kept A's why.

units.why: The guidelines "reflect emerging best practices and examples from peer institutions", which shows benchmarking against peers; P88 fits, while the consultation clause was coded separately as P84.
units.anchor: reflect emerging best practices and examples from peer institutions
units.fit_note: Reports that the guidelines reflect peer practice (benchmarking), not a partnership or coalition.
units.resolution_why: Found only by coder B (P88). The source says the guidelines 'reflect emerging best practices and examples from peer institutions', a real statement distinct from the consultation clause (P84). Kept as P88 with a fit note.

units.why: The announcement says the guidelines "are not a policy" but "a shared framework"; this scopes the whole document as an advisory framework for AI in teaching, so it is P56 (framework statement), informs, general phase, neutral stance.
units.anchor: these guidelines are not a policy
units.frag_end: navigating the use of AI in teaching and learning
units.policy: The guidelines are not a policy; they are intended to support faculty decision making and provide a shared framework for navigating the use of AI in teaching and learning.
units.fit_note: Also says the guidelines are explicitly advisory, not a policy.
units.resolution_why: Both coded P56, informs, general, neutral. Actor differed: A 'all', B 'admin'. The passage is the Provost office describing its own guidelines, so admin. Wording follows the source ('support faculty decision making and provide a shared framework for navigating the use of AI in teaching and learning').

units.why: "Faculty retain full discretion to determine whether, how, and when AI tools are used in their courses" hands the decision to each instructor, so it is P04, addressed to instructors, before-course, may.
units.anchor: Faculty retain full discretion to determine whether, how, and when AI tools are used
units.resolution_why: Both coded P04, instructor, before-course, may. unit_stance differed: A 'permit', B 'neutral'. The passage hands the decision to instructors and states no position on AI itself, consistent with the document stance 'delegates', so neutral.

units.why: "Because instructional approaches and disciplinary contexts vary widely" is the reason given for issuing guidelines instead of a policy; no type covers this justification for non-uniformity, so UNCOVERED rather than stretching P04 or P83.
units.anchor: instructional approaches and disciplinary contexts vary widely
units.uncovered_note: Explains that the university gives no uniform rule because teaching approaches and disciplines differ widely.
units.resolution_why: Found only by coder B (UNCOVERED). The source gives the reason for issuing guidelines rather than a policy: 'Because instructional approaches and disciplinary contexts vary widely, these guidelines are not a policy.' It is a real rationale; no type covers justification for non-uniformity, so UNCOVERED stays.

units.why: "We ask only that instructors clearly communicate their expectations regarding AI use in course syllabi" asks every instructor to state AI expectations in the syllabus; P09 with modality should because it is phrased as a request.
units.anchor: instructors clearly communicate their expectations regarding AI use in course syllabi
units.frag_start: We ask only that instructors clearly
units.resolution_why: Both coded P09, instructor, course-start. Modality differed: A 'must', B 'should'. The source says 'We ask only that instructors clearly communicate', a request rather than a mandate, so should.

units.why: The guidelines "feature the "traffic light" model (green, yellow, red)" to express "permissible, limited, or prohibited uses", a named tier scheme, so P05.
units.anchor: the "traffic light" model (green, yellow, red)
units.policy: The guidelines feature the "traffic light" model (green, yellow, red) to help instructors articulate permissible, limited, or prohibited uses of AI tools, particularly generative AI tools, within individual courses.
units.resolution_why: Both coded P05, instructor, before-course, informs. Normalized policy follows the source wording.

units.why: The Academic Integrity principle says "Faculty should clearly define expectations for AI use in assignments so students understand what is permitted"; this is a duty to state expectations, closest to P09 (statements in syllabus or assignment) rather than P66, since it requires no reasons to be given.
units.anchor: Faculty should clearly define expectations for AI use in assignments
units.resolution_why: Both coded P09, instructor, course-start, should; the sentence asks faculty to set expectations and does not itself classify misuse, so P09 not P36.

units.why: The same principle wants students to understand "what constitutes academic dishonesty", tying AI rules to integrity; P36 is nearest but the text does not say unauthorized use is misconduct, only that expectations separate permitted use from dishonesty.
units.anchor: what constitutes academic dishonesty
units.frag_start: so students understand what is permitted
units.policy: Students are to understand what AI use is permitted and what constitutes academic dishonesty.
units.fit_note: Does not state outright that unauthorized AI use is misconduct.
units.resolution_why: Both coded P36 with a fit note. Actor differed: A 'student', B 'all'. The source says expectations are set 'so students understand ... what constitutes academic dishonesty', so the stated beneficiary is students; student kept. The text does not say unauthorized use is misconduct, so the partial fit is kept. A's normalized policy kept because the anchor alone is not a full statement.

units.why: The Pedagogical Choice principle says faculty "align AI use with course learning objectives and disciplinary norms"; the alignment criterion makes this P83, not just P04.
units.anchor: align AI use with course learning objectives and disciplinary norms
units.resolution_why: Both coded P83, instructor, before-course, may. Agreed.

units.why: The same principle calls the traffic light model "a decision support tool", so the tiers are optional help, not a mandated scheme; coded P05 with a note.
units.anchor: using the traffic light model as a decision support tool
units.fit_note: The tiers are advisory decision support, not a required scheme.
units.resolution_why: Both coded P05 with the fit note that the tiers are decision support. Agreed.

units.why: The Responsible Use principle says "All users are expected to engage with AI tools ethically, with attention to data privacy, intellectual property, and institutional policies"; it binds everyone to ethics, privacy, IP and existing policy. P77 (follow existing policy) fits best; P50 does not because no concrete data protection is stated.
units.anchor: expected to engage with AI tools ethically
units.fit_note: Mainly an ethics expectation; the reference to institutional policies is brief.
units.resolution_why: A coded the whole Responsible Use sentence as one P77 unit; B split it into P77, P50 and P52. The codebook says one policy per unit and never merge distinct rules, so the sentence is split. This unit keeps ethical use and existing institutional policies (P77).

units.why: The same principle asks for "attention to data privacy", a privacy concern about AI use; P50 fits partly since it names no specific data rule.
units.anchor: attention to data privacy
units.fit_note: Only names data privacy; gives no specific data rule.
units.resolution_why: Found only by coder B. The same sentence asks for 'attention to data privacy', a distinct concern. A folded it into P77 and noted P50 does not fit. Kept as a separate unit under P50 with a partial-fit note, because a reader looking for privacy rules would look there.

units.why: The principle also asks for attention to "intellectual property", which P52 covers; the fit is partial as nothing specific is said.
units.anchor: intellectual property
units.fit_note: Only names intellectual property without specifics.
units.resolution_why: Found only by coder B. The same sentence asks for attention to 'intellectual property'; A folded it into P77. Kept as a separate unit under P52 with a partial-fit note.

units.why: The action item "Include a clear statement on AI use for the upcoming term" directs instructors to put an AI statement in their syllabi, which is P09, at course start.
units.anchor: Include a clear statement on AI use for the upcoming term
units.resolution_why: Both coded P09, instructor, course-start, should. Agreed.

units.why: "Sample language and templates are provided in the guidelines document" is a support the institution supplies for syllabus statements; no type covers provided templates, so UNCOVERED rather than a stretch to P09.
units.anchor: Sample language and templates are provided in the guidelines document
units.policy: Sample language and templates for syllabus AI statements are provided in the guidelines document.
units.uncovered_note: The institution supplies sample syllabus language and templates to help instructors write AI statements. (Coder B considered P63 support-faculty: support here is templates only, not learning about AI.)
units.resolution_why: A coded UNCOVERED, B coded P63 with a fit note. P63 is about helping faculty learn AI; this passage provides templates for syllabus statements, which fits only loosely. The codebook prefers UNCOVERED over a stretched fit, so UNCOVERED. Actor differed (A instructor, B admin): the guidelines document provides the templates, so admin.

units.why: "We welcome ongoing feedback as questions, concerns, and effective practices emerge" invites feedback on the guidelines, which is P54 (feedback invited).
units.anchor: We welcome ongoing feedback as questions, concerns, and effective practices emerge
units.resolution_why: Both coded P54, all, over-time, informs. Agreed.

units.why: Feedback is directed to two named people, identifying who maintains the guidelines; P80 fits partly because they are contacts rather than an enforcing office.
units.anchor: Feedback can be sent to
units.policy: Feedback on the guidelines can be sent to Crystal Williams and Kyle Pokorny.
units.fit_note: Names the people who receive feedback; P54 does not cover contact channels. Coder B coded P80, but these are feedback contacts, not an enforcing or exception-granting office.
units.resolution_why: Found only by coder B (P80). The source says 'Feedback can be sent to Crystal Williams and Kyle Pokorny', a real statement about the feedback channel. P80 is for owner, enforcement and exceptions, so it fits worse than P54 (feedback invited). Kept as P54 with a fit note.

units.why: "we will continue to update them based on technological advancements and community feedback" commits the university to revising the guidelines, a P54 revisit commitment.
units.anchor: we will continue to update them based on technological advancements and community feedback
units.resolution_why: Both coded P54, admin, over-time, informs. Agreed.

units.why: "we are also sharing links to resources within the guidelines document, including how other universities have handled this challenge" points faculty to peer practice; P88 (peers) is nearest, though it is a resource list.
units.anchor: how other universities have handled this challenge
units.frag_start: Given that we are a community
units.fit_note: Offers resource links to faculty, including peer examples, not coalitions or partnerships.
units.resolution_why: Both coded P88, admin, informs. Phase differed: A 'general', B 'before-course'. The passage describes resources supplied to faculty with the guidelines, which is institutional set-up, so before-course.

units.why: The guidelines cover AI "in the classroom and in academic administration", which sets their scope; P61 fits partly since no definition of AI is given.
units.anchor: in the classroom and in academic administration
units.frag_start: UMBC's guidelines for the use of
units.fit_note: States scope only; no definition of AI.
units.resolution_why: A coded P56, B coded P61. The source says the guidelines are 'for the use of artificial intelligence (AI) tools in the classroom and in academic administration', a statement of scope. P61 (define AI and the policy's scope) fits; P56 is already used for the framework statement. P61, with a fit note that no definition of AI is given.

units.why: The action item "Review the Full Guidelines" asks instructors to read the guidelines document; P102 (stay informed) is nearest but it concerns the guidance itself rather than AI developments.
units.anchor: Review the Full Guidelines
units.policy: Instructors review the full guidelines document.
units.fit_note: Asks for review of the guidelines document itself, not of AI developments generally.
units.resolution_why: Found only by coder A (P102). The source lists the action item 'Review the Full Guidelines: The full document is available here.' It is a real directive to instructors. P102 is nearest (stay informed) though it concerns the guidance document itself. Kept with fit note.

notes: Only the Provost announcement was coded; the full guidelines file is behind my.UMBC login (inaccessible), so units rely on summary wording. Reconciled from coders A and B. B-only P11 unit ('within individual courses', fit note: tiers used within individual courses but no statement that rules do not carry over) was dropped because the passage does not say a course rule applies only to that course. Other fit/uncovered notes were kept or merged into the final units.
